short: West Germany's Cold War tank and the benchmark for European armour since.
full:
The first series Leopard 2 was handed over to the Bundeswehr on 24 October 1979, after the collapse of the joint American-German MBT-70 project left both countries to build their own. It paired spaced multilayer armour with a Rheinmetall 120 mm smoothbore gun and a 1,500 hp MTU engine that made a 55-tonne tank capable of 68 km/h. The United States adopted the same gun for the M1A1, so most of NATO ended up firing common ammunition.

Successive versions added heavier frontal armour and a longer L55 gun. Around twenty countries have bought it, including the Netherlands, Spain, Poland, Canada and Turkey, and Germany's willingness to license or resell it has made the Leopard 2 the default European tank. Turkish Leopards took losses to anti-tank missiles in Syria in 2016, and Germany, Poland, Norway and others transferred Leopard 2A4s and A6s to Ukraine from early 2023.
